features.name: Comic shelf
features.does: Every comic on the phone in one place, with its cover, where it came from, its pages and its size, and READ, EDIT or REMOVE (remove asks twice).

features.name: Import your own comics
features.where: COMIC → Shelf → IMPORT A COMIC / IMPORT A FOLDER
features.does: Reads a CBZ, a PDF, single pictures or a whole folder of page pictures, and keeps them on the phone.
features.note: PDFs stop at 400 pages, and it says so.

features.name: CBR and other archives explained
features.does: A real CBR, CB7 or CBT file is explained in plain words, with how to turn it into a CBZ; a .cbr that is secretly a zip is read normally.
features.note: True RAR files still can't be opened in a browser.

features.name: The reader
features.does: Full-screen reading: turn pages by key, swipe, side tap, arrow keys or slider, with zoom by +/−, pinch and double tap.

features.name: Guided view
features.does: One panel at a time, filling the screen in reading order; the panels are found on the page automatically.
features.note: Panel finding can miss on pages with no clear white gaps; it then shows the whole page.

features.name: Two-page spread
features.where: Reader on a tablet or computer → TWO PAGES
features.does: Two pages side by side like a real book, with the cover on its own.

features.name: Manga mode
features.does: Reads right to left: guided panels, the page pair, swipes, taps and arrows all flip; remembered for that book.

features.name: Remembered place
features.does: Opens each comic where he stopped, down to the panel.

features.name: Public-domain library
say: find me some old western comics
features.does: Searches about 2,200 public-domain comics at the Internet Archive; the first tap says the size, the second downloads on Wi-Fi only, and the credit stays on the shelf.
features.note: Digital Comic Museum isn't used: it has no open listing and its downloads need an account.

features.name: Make a comic from an idea
say: make me a comic about a cat who wants to fly
draw a comic where a robot can't dance
features.does: Writes and draws a cover plus four pages with a hero, a friend and a rival, a beginning, two failed tries, a turn and an ending with a callback joke.
features.note: One tested story shape with varied names, places and jokes; no other genres yet.

features.name: Characters that stay the same
features.does: Each character keeps their name and look (person, cat, dog, robot, ghost, alien, bear or rabbit, plus colours, hair, hat, glasses) in every panel; rename them or give one a new look.

features.name: Proper comic lettering
features.does: Real panel grids, speech balloons with tails, thought clouds, shout and whisper balloons, caption boxes and big sound effects, with balloons never over faces.

features.name: Edit anything
features.does: Change any line, who says it, the balloon kind, the caption, the sound effect, the place, the time of day, the shot, who is in it and their face, pose, position and direction; add or remove panels, lines and pages; change the grid; edit the cover.

features.name: The script
features.does: The whole comic as a readable script, page by page.

features.name: Save and share
features.where: COMIC → Make → SAVE CBZ / SAVE PDF / SHARE
features.does: A real comic file any comic app opens, a PDF, or the phone's share sheet (it saves the PDF if sharing isn't possible).

features.name: Quick strip in Creative
features.does: The older four-panel strip, now with a MAKE A WHOLE COMIC key that jumps to the Comic app.

features.name: Comic on the MAKE hub and in Every screen
features.where: MAKE → EDITORS card; Every screen → Comic card
features.does: Shows how many comics are on the shelf and offers 'make a comic', 'read a comic' and 'free comics'.

upward.idea: More story shapes and genres: mystery, space adventure, heist, romance, spooky, sports final
upward.why: Every comic stops feeling like the same plot with new names
upward.builds_on: The comic writer and its beat structure

upward.idea: Let the brain write the script, with the app still drawing it
upward.why: Smarter, funnier stories about exactly his idea, with characters that still look the same
upward.builds_on: The comic writer and the free models the brain already uses

upward.idea: Longer comics: chapters, an issue 2 that continues issue 1, a series shelf
upward.why: A real ongoing series with the same cast
upward.builds_on: The saved cast and comic format

upward.idea: Undo and redo in the editor
Drag balloons, characters and sound effects with a finger
upward.why: Exact placement, like a pro comic tool
upward.builds_on: The tap-to-find panel and balloon map

upward.idea: More drawing: new poses, props, vehicles, animals, weather, speed lines and close-up hands
His own photo as a panel background
upward.why: Comics set in his real kitchen, street or holiday
upward.builds_on: Import and the editor (his photos stay on the phone)

upward.idea: A character maker that draws a cartoon of him or someone he introduces, with their permission
upward.why: He and his people star in their own comics
upward.builds_on: Character looks and the Faces feature (only him and people he introduces)

upward.idea: Reader polish: page-turn animation, a strip of page thumbnails, bookmarks, night reading tint, auto-advance
upward.why: As smooth as the best paid comic readers

upward.idea: Better panel finding: dark pages, borderless art, odd shapes, and fixing a panel by hand
upward.why: Guided view works on almost every real comic

upward.idea: Shelf search, sort, collections, series grouping, and read/unread marks
upward.why: Handles a library of hundreds of comics

upward.idea: Read aloud in guided mode, with each character's line in a different phone voice
upward.why: Comics for when his eyes are busy, or for kids
upward.builds_on: The reader's panels and the phone's own voices

upward.idea: Export as a phone-ready vertical scroll (webtoon style) and as single panel pictures
upward.why: Easy to post and to read on a phone

upward.idea: Open real RAR comics with a free, offline unpacker added to the app

Comic-style recap of his week or trip from his own agenda and photos

sideways.idea: Explainer comics: any topic or how-to as a short comic
sideways.why: Learn or teach something in a friendly way
sideways.builds_on: The writer, plus School and Learn

sideways.why: Quick funny pictures to share, posted only with APPROVE

sideways.idea: Greeting-card comics: a birthday or thank-you as a 3-panel comic
sideways.builds_on: The comic plus Creative's birthday card

sideways.idea: A reading log and stats: comics read, pages and time, kept on the phone
Manga and public-domain newspaper strips added to the library from other open archives
Comic-book versions of public-domain classics (Sherlock Holmes, Aesop)
sideways.why: Famous stories in a new form
sideways.builds_on: The writer, plus the Library's free books

sideways.idea: Turn any story or diary entry he writes into a comic
sideways.why: His own words become a comic

sideways.idea: Print-ready booklet export (pages arranged to fold and staple)
Comic translation: retype balloon text into another language
